newsitem.title: INDIA: India Hi-Tech up 10 pct after results.
newsitem.headline: India Hi-Tech up 10 pct after results.

text.p: Shares of India oil services firm Hi-Tech Driling surged 5.50 rupees, or nearly 10 percent, to 62.75 at the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) after the company announced a sharp surge in its 1996/97 net profit, traders said.
The stock hit a daily price limit of 10 percent at the BSE in volumes of 27,800 shares.
The company last week said its net profit in the year ending March 31, 1997 jumped 109 percent to 118.4 million rupees from 56.7 million in the year-ago period.
The firm's income from operations increased to 643.1 million rupees from 487.9 million rupees.
"The results are above expectations," said an analyst at a foreign brokerage. "We were expecting a net profit of about 83 million rupees."
Hi-Tech shares were unchanged at 58.55 rupees on the National Stock Exchange, with the stock attracting only buyers, traders said.
